Summarize multiScaleR objects

Source: R/print_methods.R
summary.multiScaleR.Rd

Summarizes output from multiScale_optim.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
summary(object, profile = FALSE, dimension = c("2d", "1d"), ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class multiScaleR.

profile

Logical. If TRUE, use profile-likelihood confidence limits for `sigma` when feasible. Defaults to FALSE so summaries remain fast; profile results are cached for repeated calls on the same fitted object during the current R session.

dimension

Character. "2d" (default) reports the radius containing prob of ideal planar kernel weight as the selected distance. "1d" restores the original distance along a line. Both definitions remain available in the returned object and printed output.

...

Optional arguments passed to the method (e.g., prob for cumulative kernel weight threshold).

Value

An object of class summary_multiScaleR. Kernel-scale limits default to Wald intervals. Scale distances, in map units, come in two forms: opt_dist (also opt_distance) holds the selected definition, which defaults to 2D rather than the 1D definition used through version 0.7.3. dimension records that selection. opt_dist_1d always holds the one-dimensional distance, the distance at which the kernel's cumulative density along a line through the point reaches prob (about 1.65 sigma for a Gaussian kernel at 90%). opt_dist_2d holds the two-dimensional distance, the radius of the circle around the point that holds prob of the weight of an ideal, untruncated kernel on a plane (about 2.15 sigma for a Gaussian kernel at 90%). Both tables have columns Mean, 2.5%, and 97.5%, and hard-radius covariates report their radius in both. See kernel_dist for when to use each. For hard-radius landscape and unweighted surface metrics, Hessian standard errors and Wald limits are shown as NA; use profile = TRUE for profile-likelihood limits. Profiling errors are reported instead of silently returning invalid limits.

Details

Set dimension = "1d" to preserve the original opt_dist and opt_distance values in existing scripts. For a dimension-independent extraction, use opt_dist_1d or opt_dist_2d. Neither selection changes the fitted sigma, coefficients, or likelihood. The 2D radius is for an ideal continuous kernel; max_D, raster edges, missing cells, and cell geometry can change the realized weight in the prepared data. See kernel_dist for formulas and examples.
